## Natural history notes

A small crambid moth characterized by narrow tan to brownish wings with darker mottling and subtle crosslines, giving it a delicate, easily overlooked appearance. In Florida, it is found in warm wooded or semi-open habitats and may be encountered near lights; records indicate adults are active through much of the year in Florida. The larval host plants and detailed life history appear to be poorly documented, so it is best treated as a small nocturnal moth whose caterpillars likely feed concealed on plant material while serving as part of the broader food web for spiders, birds, bats, and other insect-eating animals.
